candidate.answerReason: The only two-digit prime palindrome is 11. The possible three-digit palindromic factors are 101 through 181 in steps of 10; exactly 101, 131, 151, and 181 are prime. They produce the four palindromic years 1111, 1441, 1661, and 1991.

methods.label: Restrict the palindromic factors
methods.explanation:
First determine the two-digit prime factor. Any two-digit palindrome has the form \(11a\), where \(a\) is a digit from \(1\) through \(9\). This is prime only when \(a=1\), so that factor must be \(11\).

Write the year as \(11p\), where \(p\) is a three-digit prime palindrome. The year bounds give
\[
1000\leq 11p\leq 2000.
\]
Since \(p\) is a three-digit integer, it follows that \(100\leq p\leq181\). A palindrome in this range starts and ends with \(1\), so the complete candidate list is
\[
101,111,121,131,141,151,161,171,181.
\]
Five candidates are composite:
\[
111=3\cdot37,\quad121=11^2,\quad141=3\cdot47,
\]
\[
161=7\cdot23,\qquad171=3\cdot57.
\]
The remaining numbers \(101,131,151,181\) are prime. To verify this, division by each of \(2,3,5,7,11,13\) leaves a nonzero remainder for all four. These tests suffice because every composite number has a prime divisor at most its square root, and all the candidates are less than \(14^2\).

Multiplying the four primes by \(11\) gives
\[
1111,\qquad1441,\qquad1661,\qquad1991.
\]
Each is a palindrome in the required range. Every possible factor was considered, and distinct factors give distinct years. Therefore there are \(\boxed{4}\) years, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
